entries.title: Tulsi Gabbard Confirmed to Run — And Downsize — ODNI
entries.summary: Sen. Mitch McConnell broke with Republicans and voted against Gabbard’s confirmation as director of national intelligence.
entries.content:
Tulsi Gabbard is set to become director of national intelligence after the Senate voted Wednesday morning to confirm her to President Donald Trump’s cabinet.

Sen. Mitch McConnell was the lone Republican to join all the Democrats in the Senate in voting against Gabbard. McConnell also voted against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s nomination last month.

“The nation should not have to worry that the intelligence assessments the President receives are tainted by a Director of National Intelligence with a history of alarming lapses in judgment,” the senator said in a statement after the Gabbard vote.
entries.author: Shifra Dayak

entries.title: RFK Jr. Is on the Precipice of Leading the U.S. Health System After a Key Senate Vote
entries.summary: The Senate voted on party lines to advance the nomination of Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
entries.content:
Two years and a few weeks ago, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. spoke at an anti-vaccine mandate rally on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial. On Wednesday, the Senate voted to advance Kennedy’s nomination for secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services, putting him at the helm of public health infrastructure in the U.S.

Only a final Senate vote now stands between Kennedy and the most powerful health position in the country. That vote will likely take place later this month.

Senators voted on party lines, 53-47.
entries.author: Margaret Manto

entries.title: How Todd Blanche Tried to Woo Democrats at His DOJ Confirmation Hearing
entries.summary: The president’s personal defense lawyer could become deputy attorney general.
entries.content:
Todd Blanche, President Donald Trump’s pick for deputy attorney general, acknowledged at his confirmation hearing on Wednesday that he remains the president’s lawyer. But he insisted that their close ties wouldn’t be a problem.

The tight-knit personal relationship he’s established with Trump over the past two years presents a major question over how he will handle the job of deputy attorney general — especially when he continues to claim that every prosecution against Trump was nothing but partisan hackery. Blanche attempted to assuage those concerns at his hearing with the Senate Judiciary Committee, including saying that his close relationship with Trump showed that their concerns about the president’s conduct were unnecessary.

“I don’t think that President Trump is going to ask me to do anything illegal or immoral,” Blanche said when asked how he would respond to an illegal order from the president.
entries.author: Jose Pagliery

entries.title: The Senate Has an 18-Year Perfect Ethics Streak, Says the Senate
entries.summary: Lawmakers are batting 0-for-1,826 in issuing “disciplinary sanctions” for alleged bad behavior.
entries.content:
The U.S. Senate Select Committee on Ethics did not formally punish anyone in 2024 — despite receiving 158 complaints that year of alleged violations of Senate rules, according to a new committee report reviewed by NOTUS.

No, not even former Sen. Robert Menendez, who a judge sentenced last month to 11 years in federal prison on a bribery conviction. Menendez skirted Senate Ethics Committee comeuppance because the committee “lost jurisdiction for its adjudicatory review” when the senator resigned in August.

With this latest report, lawmakers officially marked the 18th year in a row that the notoriously secretive committee failed to formally punish anyone within its jurisdiction, which includes Senate staffers and senators.
entries.author: Dave Levinthal
